construct: When single-nephron filtration and proximal luminal flow increase, absolute proximal sodium and bicarbonate reabsorption rises so that fractional reabsorption remains relatively stable. Proximal-tubule brush-border microvilli act as flow sensors; increased shear/torque promotes NHE3 trafficking and transport activity, coupling tubular reabsorption to filtered load.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A rise in filtered load with proportional rise in proximal absolute reabsorption and stable fractional reabsorption defines glomerulotubular balance. Flow sensing by proximal brush-border microvilli promotes NHE3 trafficking/activity.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Basolateral Na/K-ATPase is necessary for proximal transport, but the offered alternative decreases its activity; the stem specifically asks the adaptive cellular response to increased luminal flow.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The experimental isolation of higher single-nephron flow with fixed hormones makes flow-dependent apical NHE3 recruitment the uniquely best adaptive mechanism.
